Ibn Saud, Abdulaziz Al Saud, was the founder and first king of Saudi Arabia. He ruled from 1902 until his death in 1953.

His family had ruled central Arabia twice before, allied with the preachers of Ibn Abd al-Wahhab's strict reform movement, but rivals had driven them into exile in Kuwait. In 1902 the young Abdulaziz retook Riyadh with a small band in a night raid.

  • He won back the Nejd and the east coast, using the Ikhwan, tribesmen settled in religious farming colonies, as his shock troops.
  • In 1924 and 1925 he took the Hejaz with Mecca and Medina from the Hashemites.
  • When the Ikhwan turned on him for dealing with the British, he crushed them in 1929.
  • He named the united kingdom Saudi Arabia in 1932.

In 1938 American geologists struck oil in commercial amounts, and the concession that became Saudi Aramco turned his poor desert kingdom into one of the richest states on earth. His sons have ruled ever since.
sum: Ibn Saud, Abdulaziz Al Saud, was the founder and first king of Saudi Arabia. He ruled from 1902 until his death in 1953.
